output.argument_summary:
1. The cleanest admissible reading is not that the named catastrophe-claim evidence-triage context has passed; it has not. The admissible record says that context is named in the deployment plan and its evals are not in the packet (ISTRESS-EVAL-COVERAGE-GAP-009-CURRENT-GAP), and the general support/latency/rollback checks do not cover it (ISTRESS-EVAL-COVERAGE-GAP-009-NEAR-MISS).
2. That does not collapse the entire certification case. Separate launch readiness from certification wording. Aggregate readiness evidence shows the release clears the launch threshold by 2.0 points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents (ISTRESS-EVAL-COVERAGE-GAP-009-AGGREGATE-PASS). That supports operational launch readiness for the tested configuration, not full named-context coverage.
3. The model-card wording is the area that needs to be constrained. The current draft statement that there are no known insurance-claims-triage limitations is not supportable as written because QA treats the missing evals as unknown rather than passed (ISTRESS-EVAL-COVERAGE-GAP-009-CONTEXT). I concede that limitation.
4. On the policy point, the policy text does not support a clean, unqualified certification record for a named deployment context with missing evaluation coverage. It does support a narrower record where the packet expressly discloses the unresolved named-context gap instead of implying it was tested or passed (ISTRESS-EVAL-COVERAGE-GAP-009-POLICY). Public governance guidance is aligned with that narrower treatment because it emphasizes documenting limitations and evaluation results and managing risk through measurement and monitoring across deployment (ISTRESS-EVAL-COVERAGE-GAP-009-HF-CONTENT; ISTRESS-EVAL-COVERAGE-GAP-009-NIST-MEASURE).
5. So the supportable position is: launch readiness evidence is sufficient for the release generally; certification language must be caveated; disclosure must say the catastrophe-claim evidence-triage coverage is still unknown in this packet; monitoring can manage residual uncertainty after launch, but monitoring is not retroactive proof that the missing eval requirement was already satisfied.
6. I am not asking the auditor to treat the gap as resolved or to infer risk acceptance. I am asking that the recommendation be interpreted as caveated certification/no escalation rather than as a clean pass, because the same admissible record supports operational readiness plus explicit disclosure, while the overreach is in any unqualified wording, not in the narrower readiness claim itself.
